newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe coup trial postponed to March.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe coup trial postponed to March.

text.p: A Zimbabwean court on Friday put off to next year the trial of veteran opposition leader Ndabaningi Sithole on charges of plotting to kill President Robert Mugabe.
Sithole, 77, last week asked the high court to postpone the trial, saying he wanted more time to prepare his defence and also to contest the basis of the law and order maintenance act.
His lawyer, Tendai Biti, charged that the information provided by the prosecution was scanty and was only given three days before the scheduled November 4 trial start.

Biti argued that the law and order maintenance act under which Sithole was charged placed the burden of proof on the accused, contrary to the constitutional guarantee that an accused person was innocent until proven guilty.

On Friday, remanding Sithole to March 17, Justice James Devittie ordered the state to provide Sithole's lawyers with statements from witnesses and said he was referring the constitutional challenge to the Supreme Court.

"I make my ruling as follows: that the state shall forthwith provide the accused with witness statements; that the following questions with regard to Section 18 of Chapter 20 of the constitution shall be referred to the Supreme Court," he said.
But he also granted the prosecution leave to appeal against his order to provide state witnesses' statements to the defence.
Devittie ordered that the state should give Sithole back his passport and Z$50,000 (U.S.$4,695) he surrendered as bail surety following his arrest last October.
Sithole is facing three charges -- possession of arms, involvement in acts of sabotage and terrorism and conspiracy to assassinate President Mugabe, his political rival for the past 30 years.
He denies the charges and accuses Mugabe of trumping them up to settle a personal vendetta.
